title: Icing: Where It Lives, How You Leave

faa.title: Pilot Guide: Flight in Icing Conditions

hook: Ice doesn't announce itself. It just starts redesigning your wing.

scenes.narration: November crossing, filed for nine thousand. Clouds ahead, outside air temp minus five. And on the leading edge — a thin, smooth sheen you almost didn't see. Kid, you've got a passenger who didn't buy a ticket.
Smooth, glassy, heavy, hard to see. Which ice is that — clear or rime? Commit.

Clear ice — the dangerous one. Why is it sneaky? Big supercooled drops FLOW BACK before they freeze, so it builds in smooth sheets that don't look like ice. Rime is the opposite: small drops, instant freeze, white and brittle. Mixed is both.
The recipe is always the same: visible moisture plus a surface at or below freezing. Zero to minus twenty Celsius — that's the kitchen you're flying through right now.

Your outs, planned BEFORE takeoff: where's the freezing level, the warm air, the clear air? One special case — freezing rain means warmer air is ABOVE you. The best de-ice equipment is the altitude where the ice isn't.
onScreenText: freezing level · warm air · clear air

scenes.narration: Eyes off the screen. The two ingredients of structural icing, and what freezing rain tells you. Out loud.
Moisture plus a freezing surface. Clear sneaks, rime crusts. File with an out, kid — hope is not an anti-ice system.
From the METAR lesson — which cloud layers make a ceiling? Quick.
A C ninety-one dash seventy-four bravo. The F A A's guide to staying warm.

quiz.question: A smooth, glassy, heavy accretion building on the leading edge is:
quiz.explanation: Clear ice flows back before freezing, building smooth heavy sheets — the most dangerous and hardest-to-see accretion type.

quiz.question: Structural icing requires:
choices: Visible moisture and aircraft surface temperature at or below freezing
quiz.explanation: Both ingredients are required: visible moisture (cloud, rain) and a surface at or below 0°C. (AC 91-74B)

quiz.question: You encounter freezing rain. The warmer air you may need is most likely:
quiz.explanation: Freezing rain forms when precipitation falls from warmer air aloft into a below-freezing layer — a climb may reach the warm layer.
